data_quality_notes:
SHAPE OF THE DAY, stated first because it is the finding and not a shortfall: this run produced ZERO new directional entries. All seven recommendations are position management — two closes (CCJ, CAG), two pending-order withdrawals (MU, /MBTU6), two holds with amended plans (TLT, LCII), and one explicit wait (NKE). Research reached RESEARCH COMPLETE inside its budget at ~39 minutes, so nothing here is truncation. Two independent reasons were documented. (1) The geometry refuses: a 2.0 ATR stop floor plus a 2:1 ratio needs about 4 ATR of room to a defensible level, and today's low-ATR leaders sit too close to their highs (XLV 1.34% ATR, 3.34% off high; QQQ 1.28%, 0.55% off high) while high-ATR names need targets larger than any level in the data supports. Rejections documented in notes.md: SOL, BTC, ETH, KMX, XLV, ITB, XRT, CCL. (2) The correlation cap binds: TLT, XLU and the pending IYR are already three ideas on the rising-long-yield driver, so the ITB and XRT shorts are refused on the cap despite working geometry. Research recorded explicitly that it declined a CCL short it could have dressed up, because the pull to publish it was about the shape of the page rather than the merit of the idea. I have not padded it back in.

THE RUN'S MOST IMPORTANT FINDING: the Federal Reserve HIKED 25bp on 2026-09-16 to a 3.75-4.00% target range, unanimously 12-0, its first increase since 2023, under chair Kevin Warsh, with a dot plot pointing to another. Verified three ways: the Kalshi contract KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H25 is finalized result YES (and the paired H0 finalized NO), FRED effective fed funds at 3.88% sits mid-band for that range, and three independent news sources. An October hike prices at 63.5% and a cut at literally zero. This is an active hiking cycle, not a higher-for-longer pause, and much of the open book is on the wrong side of it. Research also flags that the stated driver is spiralling oil, which makes the energy longs (XLE, DINO, pending OXY) and the rate shorts (TLT, XLU, IYR) one trade seen from both ends: six positions on one oil-to-CPI-to-hikes impulse, where the correlation counter scores them as two sleeves of three. That is the next run's first job.

PRICES. Today is Sunday 2026-09-27. Every equity and ETF price here is the 2026-09-25 (Friday) close from finnhub, session 'closed', age ~2,319 minutes (~38.7h). That is a closed market, not stale data. I re-quoted all six equity symbols at synthesis and every one matched the figure captured during research, so nothing was revised. The BTC proxy price for the /MBTU6 withdrawal (84,748) is live from CoinGecko.

RATIOS RECOMPUTED. Only two ideas have a computable ratio; the other five are exits, withdrawals or a wait, and carry none by construction. TLT: from the filled 81.87 entry, a 78.00 target against the 83.30 stop is 3.87/1.43 = 2.71:1, clearing the 2.0 swing floor, against a break-even hit rate of 27.0% and a claimed 58% win probability. LCII: from the filled 94.00 entry, the 138 target against a defended 65 bear case is 44/29 = 1.52:1, which FAILS the 2.5 long_term floor. I am publishing that failure rather than engineering around it: a filled entry cannot be rewritten to make a ratio work, the recommendation is hold-do-not-add rather than buy, and demotion to the watchlist by the enforcement pass is the correct outcome. The value of the amendment is that it attaches the invalidation condition the position has never carried (net margin below 3% for two consecutive quarters, a dividend cut, or a current ratio below 2.0). No ratio here clusters just above its floor — there are only two of them, one comfortably clear and one openly failing.

STOP DISTANCE, checked the other way. One honest flag on the top-ranked idea: measured against today's ATR14 of 0.8039, TLT's unchanged 83.30 stop is 1.43 points or 1.78 ATR from the 81.87 filled entry, a hair under the 1.8 ETF floor. I have not moved it. The entry is filled and cannot be amended; from spot the stop is 4.95 ATR away while the target is 1.64 ATR away, so the position is not exposed to ordinary daily range; and widening a winning short's stop to satisfy a floor computed against an ATR that has changed since publication would make the trade worse to make a check pass. Flagging it for the red team rather than quietly fixing it. Research's own systematic sweep of all 13 open positions with price history found worse: SNX was published with a stop 1.39 ATR from entry against a 2.0 floor, and XLE (0.92 ATR from spot), CEG (1.48) and DINO (1.74) are now very exposed. Distance from spot compresses as a trade moves against you and is a risk statement rather than a rule violation, but the CCJ close is precisely this problem judged to be terminal.

ONE EDIT I MADE TO A CANDIDATE, declared: LCII arrived with an entry zone of 78-88 sitting beneath its own 94.00 fill, which contradicts the same candidate's explicit instruction not to average down. I removed the zone and made the prohibition an entry condition. Nothing else was changed beyond prepending the position-update sentence the four open-position amendments needed.

CONVICTION. Every score equals the count of distinct evidence kinds, with one deliberate exception. TLT is the only 5 and has four kinds including a settled primary document. Five ideas at 4 carry three kinds each. LCII carries three kinds, which the table scores as a 4, and research set it to 3 on purpose because the position has no insider support in either direction and its ratio fails from the filled entry. check_conviction_evidence will therefore report a supported score of 4 against a stated 3 — that flag is expected and should NOT be corrected upward. The documented failure mode is inflation, not caution.

COVERAGE GAPS AND FAILED SOURCES. No VIX, DXY, gold spot, WTI, SPX/NDX/RUT or index-futures level today: finnhub refuses indices without a CFD subscription, yahoo returned 429 on all quotes and history and 401 on options, stooq returned 404 and is now behind a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge (not circumvented, by design). TWO TOOLING BUGS FOUND, WITH FIXES, because they have been silently degrading event-contract coverage. (1) market_data.py events fetches only the first 200 open Kalshi markets unsorted and filters client-side, so every macro query returns sports; the fix is to pass series_ticker to /markets (KXFEDDECISION, KXCPI, KXCPIYOY, KXU3, KXRECSSNBER). (2) The /markets list returns yes_bid, yes_ask and last_price as null for every market, which is why event contracts have looked unpriceable; real prices are in /markets/{ticker}/orderbook. Also worth a guard: merge_report's one-position-per-(symbol, direction) rule treats sell and sell_short as different directions, so the open TLT SELL and the pending TLT SELL_SHORT are one view tracked as two positions; and nothing caught two mutually exclusive event contracts on the same FOMC meeting being carried at once. A method note for anyone re-deriving crypto figures: CoinGecko /coins/{id}/ohlc must be called with days=30, which returns 4-hourly data; days=90 returns 4-day buckets and yields an ATR roughly double the true daily figure.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT. 8 closed of 40 tracked, 1 of 8 hitting target, average -3.2%. That sample is far under the ~15 closed trades needed to mean anything and should not be over-fitted. What is not noise is the pattern research identified in the stop-distance sweep: the closed losses share tight stops, and the structural finding of the day is that those stops cannot be widened after a fill without breaking the ratio that justified publishing the idea. That is the honest reason two of today's seven recommendations are closes.

A SECOND DECLARED EDIT: the two pending-order withdrawals arrived treated differently — MU carried catalyst.wait true and /MBTU6 carried false. Both are withdrawals with a null entry, so neither can fill and neither should open a tracked position; I set /MBTU6 to wait true to match MU. A cancelled order is the clearest case there is of 'do not enter'.

WHAT I VERIFIED RATHER THAN TOOK ON TRUST. The whole report rests on the Fed having hiked, and that
evidence was flagged with a source failure, so it was the first thing checked. All four Kalshi
endpoints return HTTP 200 on re-fetch: KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H25 is status finalized, result yes,
expiration_value 'Hike 25bps'; the paired H0 is finalized result no; 26OCT-H25 is active at 63 bid /
64 ask; 26DEC-H25 at 68/69. Every figure synthesis published off those contracts is exact. TLT's
technicals were re-derived from a fresh 130-bar pull and also match to the share: ATR14 0.8039,
SMA20 81.369, SMA50 82.2472, range 78.83-87.79, -9.65% off high, +0.62% off low, and the escalating
volumes 53,502,360 / 59,160,590 / 62,576,660 with the 78.83 low printed on 2026-09-25. All six equity
quotes re-quoted unchanged. So the two `sources` FAIL flags are BOTH FALSE and must not be read as
fabrication: the Kalshi 404s were transient, and every nasdaq 404 (CCJ, MU, LCII, and TLT's technical
leg) is a citation-form defect — `api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical` does not resolve without
the query parameters that market_data.py actually sends, so the URL written into `sources` is a stem,
not a dead source. Worth fixing in the research phase; not grounds to kill an idea.

CUT: /MBTU6, from rank 6 to the watchlist in full. A terminated contract, catalyst dated two days in
the past, no entry, no target, no stop, carried at conviction 4. The content was right and the
placement was wrong — cancelling a dead order is housekeeping, not a recommendation, and a 'short'
row on an expired instrument is misreadable as live.

FIXED, and this is the finding of the pass: CAG and CCJ would each have opened a phantom SHORT
position. Both say in their own text 'this is an exit, not a short', and both carried direction sell
with catalyst.wait false and an entry price at spot. merge_report keys on (symbol, direction); the
live positions are CAG buy and CCJ buy, so ('CAG','sell') and ('CCJ','sell') matched nothing and
opened new rows. Simulated against state/open_positions.json before the fix: 'opened 2, amended 0',
CAG sell pending at 14.32 and CCJ sell pending at 88.07, each with target None and stop None. This
bug has already fired once and is in the performance record — 2026-09-08's NKE exit recommendation at
38.40 is sitting in state as an open, filled NKE SELL position with no target and no stop, which is
not a trade anyone took. Today's NKE rec endorses that row ('any existing exit recommendation at
38.40 stands'), so it will persist until someone corrects the state file; recorded here rather than
corrected, because rewriting stored history is not this phase's job. The fix applied is
catalyst.wait true on both, which is what MU and /MBTU6 already used for exactly this reason — a
withdrawal is the clearest case of 'do not enter', and a close is the same case with a price attached.
Verified after the fix: opened 0, amended 0, and both longs keep their own target and stop. Flipping
direction to buy to force an amendment was tested and rejected: it writes a {target None, stop None}
amendment onto each filled long, stripping CAG's 16.74/14.20 and CCJ's 135.00/82.50 and leaving two
positions that grading can never close. The entry zones were removed from both for the same reason
synthesis removed LCII's — an entry zone on an exit row is an invitation to put on the opposite trade.

FIXED: TLT's entry zone, which is the same defect on the highest-conviction idea on the page, where it
does the most damage. The row advertised zone 79.30-81.90 against a spot of 79.32 — the zone's lower
bound was spot — while publishing 2.71:1. That ratio holds only from the 2026-09-02 fill at 81.87.
From spot the identical 78.00 target and 83.30 stop are 1.32 points of reward against 3.98 of risk:
0.33:1, a break-even hit rate of 75.1%, and at the stated 58% win probability an expectancy of -0.91
points, -0.23R. A reader entering in the advertised zone would take a negative-expectancy trade off a
row reading 2.71:1. Zone removed, ideal kept at 81.87 as the fill it is, with the prohibition made an
entry condition. The 58% was also justified against the wrong denominator: the 27.0% break-even comes
from entry-to-target versus entry-to-stop, while the 58% was argued from spot-to-target versus
spot-to-stop. Stated consistently, the 4.95 ATR distance to the stop is not asymmetry — it is the
reason there is little payoff left. Levels themselves untouched: the 78.00 target was NOT moved out
and the 83.30 stop was NOT moved in, which is the manipulation this phase exists to catch.

DOWNGRADED: TLT conviction 5 to 4, the only 5 on the page and the one that would be sized largest.
check_conviction_evidence passes it on four distinct kinds and it is right about the labels, but it
counts kinds and cannot see that two pairs collapse. primary_document (the settled September FOMC
contract) and dated_catalyst (the active October contract) are one fact — the Fed is hiking — read off
the same exchange's same series, backward and forward. technical_level and the volume half of
positioning are one observation off one nasdaq price series, and 'positioning' carries no positioning
data at all: the report states plainly that short interest and days-to-cover failed for every name.
What remains is two genuinely independent confirmations — Kalshi/FRED on the hiking cycle, and TLT's
own tape breaking down — plus the FRED 10s2s bear steepener as a third that is real but macro rather
than positioning. That is a 4. Also relevant to the size: the thesis is now fully public. The hike was
eleven days ago, an October hike prices at 63.5% and a cut at zero, and the position is already +3.1%.
Being right and being early are different, and this is the former.

NOT CHANGED, deliberately, because cutting to look busy is as harmful as missing something.
LCII stays exactly as published, failing at 1.52:1 against the 2.5 long_term floor. Synthesis is right
that a filled entry cannot be rewritten to rescue a ratio and right to publish the failure for the
enforcement pass to demote rather than engineer around it; the amendment's value is the invalidation
condition the position never had. I add only that LCII is an open long 2.1% above a 52-week low with
no stop of any kind, which the row does say. NKE's wait stands: refusing to trade a binary event with
no ATR to place a stop from is correct, and the opportunity cost is named honestly in key_risk. MU's
withdrawal stands, with one mechanical note — wait true means the tracker skips it, so publishing this
does NOT remove the pending MU buy at 960 from state; that order has to be cancelled at the broker,
and the row is advisory. CORRELATION TEST: no cut. Today's only maintained directional exposure is
TLT short duration; everything else is an exit, a withdrawal or a wait, and two of the six actions
(CAG, CCJ) reduce gross exposure. The six-position oil-to-CPI-to-hikes cluster synthesis identified
is real and is a property of the open book rather than of today's recommendations, and the right place
to act on it is the next run, as synthesis said.

RE-RANKED by what needs an order placed rather than by conviction, because every row is position

market_context.summary: An active hiking cycle that the book had not priced, and a tape splitting cleanly along it. The Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, unanimously 12-0 — its first increase since 2023 — with a dot plot pointing to another and a chair committed to a timelier return to 2%; October prices at 63.5% for a further hike and 0% for a cut, December at 68.5%. The 10-year is 5.18% and rising, with 10s2s bear-steepening from 0.31 to 0.36, so the long end is repricing faster than the front. The resulting internals are the most useful fact available today: mega-cap tech and semis sit at their highs (QQQ 0.55% off its 120-day high, SMH above both averages) while everything rate-sensitive and domestically cyclical rolls over (IWM -7.6%, ITB -15.9%, XRT -11.8%, XLF and KRE both below both averages). Banks are notably NOT working despite the steepener, which kills the textbook NIM trade on evidence. The stated driver of the hike is inflation from spiralling oil, which means the energy longs and the rate shorts in this book are one trade viewed from two ends rather than two diversified sleeves.
